survivors_flagged.one_line: Cintas deal at $155 cash + 0.772 CTAS, worth about $311 against UNF at $260.85, a gross spread of about 19% pricing heavy FTC risk. Shareholders approved 6/11, both firms certified Second Request compliance 10/2, and they agreed not to close before Dec 11 unless the FTC closes its probe first. The FTC decision or suit by about mid-Dec is the dated binary; Canada's review is also in progress.

50/50 Viva Aerobus combination (Grupo Mas Vuelos): shareholders, FTC and Colombia have cleared it. Mexico's antitrust ruling (>75% domestic share) is the last gate, expected before end-2026. Real binary, but a merger of equals with no arb spread.

verified.catalyst: The FTC will either clear Cintas's acquisition of UniFirst ($155 cash plus 0.772 CTAS shares per UNF share) or sue to block it, with the Second Request waiting period and the reported Dec-11 no-close date putting that decision around mid-December 2026.
verified.dated_milestone: Second Requests issued 2026-06-11 and UNF shareholders approved the same day (confirmed). Triage says both firms certified substantial compliance on 10/2, which would end the 30-day HSR clock around early November, and that they agreed not to close before 12/11; I could not verify either claim. Next date: FTC clearance or complaint, expected by about 2026-12-11. Canada's Competition Bureau review is also open.
verified.instrument: UNF common, long only or hedged by shorting 0.772 CTAS per UNF share. The hedge locks the $155 cash leg plus the stock leg.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes: named counterparty Cintas, signed merger agreement 2026-03-11. G2 yes: fixed $155 cash + 0.772 CTAS consideration, shareholder approval obtained, $213M termination fee reported. G3 yes: specific unpriced figure is the ~19.3% gross spread ($311.26 deal value vs $260.85).
verified.edge: M-L. The event is real, contractual and dated, but the market already prices it as roughly a coin flip on the FTC. With a break price near the pre-leak base of about $200, the implied close probability is about 55%. Uniform rental is concentrated (Cintas is #1, UNF is #3), so heavy FTC risk is a reasonable view rather than mispricing. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base ($199.84 on 2026-02-09, before the 02-10 approach news) to today: +30.5%. Remaining to deal value ($155 + 0.772 x $202.41 = $311.26): +19.3%. So the event is not mostly harvested, and about 40% of the original gap is still on the table. UNF has also fallen from its 50-day average of ~$274 to $260.85. The spread widening recently is a mild negative signal on regulatory odds.
verified.primary_source: UniFirst news release on the Second Request and shareholder approval, 2026-06-11 (investors.unifirst.com/node/20606); MLex on the HSR waiting period, 2026; FMP batch quote UNF $260.85 / CTAS $202.41, 2026-10-12; FMP EOD UNF price history, Jan-Mar 2026
verified.analysis: This is a clean, contractual cash-plus-stock merger arb, so the numerator-provenance rule does not apply. Using CTAS at $202.41, the deal is worth $311.26 against UNF at $260.85: a 19.3% gross spread that resolves within about two months on an FTC binary. Downside if the deal breaks is roughly $195-200, the pre-approach trading range, so the trade risks about $61-66 to make about $50 (reward/risk ~0.8). That is fair-to-slightly-favorable only if you put FTC clearance above roughly 55-60%. Gap: the web-search budget ran out before I could confirm the 10/2 compliance certification or the Dec-11 timing agreement. The only sources found run through August, and FMP press releases since 09-15 show nothing deal-related. Hold at WATCH until those two items are confirmed and there is any read on FTC staff posture (a consent or divestiture remedy versus a suit).

verified.catalyst: Mexico's antitrust authority (CNA, which replaced COFECE) still has to rule on the 50/50 holding-company merger of equals between Volaris and Viva Aerobus (combined about 69% of domestic passengers). This is the last major closing condition.
verified.dated_milestone: Announced about 2025-12-19. Volaris shareholders approved on 2026-03-25 (91.8% of share capital in favour). Management guided to regulatory review taking up to 12 months from announcement, which points to a CNA ruling by about Dec 2026. No date has been set. Next datable checkpoint: Q3-2026 earnings in late October 2026.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes: the counterparty is named (Viva Aerobus / Grupo Mas Vuelos). G2 partial: a signed merger agreement plus a shareholder vote, but the Mexican regulatory outcome is open and remedies are possible. G3 fails: there is no cash price, exchange-ratio premium or quantified synergy figure that sits unpriced against today's price, so there is no contractual numerator.
verified.edge: L. This is an all-share merger of equals: no arbitrage spread, no premium, and no contractual price to anchor favourable-resolution value. Any upside would come from synergies or pricing power that I could not quantify within the lookup budget, so no provenance-checked number exists. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about -22%. The stock closed at $7.95 on 2025-12-17, jumped to $9.49 on announcement (2025-12-19) and is $6.23 now (FMP, 2026-10-12), near its 52-week low of $5.79. Nothing has been harvested; the move since announcement is fuel- and operations-driven, not deal-related. Remaining to favourable resolution: not derivable. Without a contractual price the remaining percentage is undefined, and approval mostly removes a risk rather than delivering a number. The $9.08 consensus target (+46%) comes from analysts and is excluded under the provenance rule.
verified.primary_source: DLA Piper, 'Volaris-Viva Aerobus merger' (2026-04-03): CNA jurisdiction, closing conditions (Mexico, HSR, Colombia), 2026-03-25 shareholder vote. Mexico Business News, CNA independence test commentary (Jan 2026). FMP quote VLRS $6.23 (2026-10-12) and EOD history (2025-12-17 $7.95, 2025-12-19 $9.49). FMP news feed 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-12: no CNA ruling reported.
verified.analysis: The binary is real, dated in rough terms and still ahead: CNA approval, probably with conditions, is the last gate. A merger of equals still has no numerator: approval does not pay the common holder a fixed amount, it only unlocks synergies nobody has quantified, and a forced remedy (slot or route divestitures at a combined 69% domestic share) could erase them. The equity has fallen about 22% below its pre-announcement base on fuel costs and fleet groundings, so the event is not priced in. But the thesis then becomes an airline-operations and fuel recovery call rather than an event, so score it as the equity, capped at 4. Gaps: the web search budget ran out after one query, so I could not confirm that the FTC/HSR waiting period and Colombian clearance are done, whether the CNA has issued a ruling, or the 10-Q net debt detail (Seeking Alpha 2026-09-23 cites net debt/EBITDAR of 3.2-3.3x and $824M liquidity; there is no preferred stock ahead of the common).
